Richard Terry notes that spotless decks, and masts and yards that "shone like silver", were the marks of a Yankee packet ship, kept that way by a terrible discipline.

source.en: R. R. Terry, The Shanty Book, Part I (London, 1921), note to No. 15, p. xv, read from the scan

Terry prints it as a halliard shanty, for hoisting the sails: the shantyman sings each line alone and the crew answers "Blow, boys blow".

source.en: R. R. Terry, The Shanty Book, Part I (1921), No. 15, pp. 32 and 33, read from the scan
